title: "hpc"

The `hpc` subcommand is used to configure HPC environments.

## Commands

```
  hpc       Master HPC setup
  hpc git
  hpc scratch
  hpc apptainer
  hpc slurm
  hpc r
```

## Installation

Assuming that the HPC is running on Linux, the following line will install `setupmjr` without requiring `sudo` permission:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/main/install-local.sh | bash
```

Confirm that installation worked by running:

```bash
setupmjr --version
```

If the above does not work, then `setupmjr` may not be on your system `PATH`. In that case, you can add the following line to your shell profile (typically `~/.bashrc`):

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

Then run:

```
source ~/.bashrc
```

At this point, the following should succeed:

```bash
setupmjr --version
```

If not, then the initial installation failed.

## Setup

The following command will configure the HPC environment:

```bash
setupmjr hpc
```

Apart from needing to edit one file for Git authentication if this has not been setup yet (see below), this command requires no other user input.

`setupmjr hpc` does the following:

- *Helps store large files effectively*: Large files are stored in the `/scratch` space (if available) rather than `/home`, to respect HPC storage policies.
- *Authenticates with Git*: Scripts are added to which the user needs to simply add their GitHub username and a personal access token (PAT) to enable seamless Git operations from the HPC environment.
- *Add `Apptainer` and `SLURM` helpers*: If these tools are available on the HPC, helper scripts will be added to simplify their usage.
- *Configures `radian`*: If you use `radian` as your R terminal, it is configured to work properly on the HPC.

Each of these features can be configured independently via the respective subcommands (`hpc scratch`, `hpc apptainer`, `hpc slurm`, `hpc git`, `hpc r`).

### Setting up Git

To configure Git, run the following command (which is also part of the `setupmjr hpc` command):

```bash
setupmjr hpc git
```

This command simply calls `setupmjr git`, which configures your Git profile (name and email) via `setupmjr git profile` and sets up authentication credentials via `setupmjr git auth`.

For full details on how this works and how it configures your environment (including setting up `.bashrc.d` and `.zshrc.d` files for seamless GitHub authentication), please refer to the [git setup documentation](git.qmd).

### Using scratch space

HPCs typically have a separate scratch space for storing large files (i.e. `/scratch/$USER`), which is often faster and has different quotas than the home directory.
The `setupmjr hpc scratch` command helps you configure your environment to use this scratch space effectively.

To set this up, run the following command (also part of `setupmjr hpc`):

```bash
setupmjr hpc scratch
```

This configures your environment to preferentially use the `/scratch` space for the following:

- Apptainer and Singularity images
  - Automatically cached in `/scratch/$USER/.cache/<apptainer/singularity>` instead of the default location in the home directory.
- R libraries:
  - The `R_LIBS_USER` environment variable is set to `/scratch/$USER/.local/lib/R` and created, so that R packages are installed in the scratch space instead of the home directory.
  - Similarly, various `RENV_*` environment variables configuring `renv` paths are set to point to the scratch space.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The `hpc scratch` command configures the environment to use the `/scratch` directory by doing the following:

1. It ensures that `.bashrc.d` files are sourced by `.bashrc`.

2. A script is added to `~/.bashrc.d/hpc-scratch.sh`, which explicitly exports paths for Apptainer, Singularity, `renv`, and R libraries to use `/scratch/$USER`. Specifically, it sets the following environment variables:
   - `RENV_CONFIG_PAK_ENABLED=false`
   - `RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED=false`
   - `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R/library`
   - `RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/scratch/${USER}/renv/cache:/renv/cache`
   - `RENV_PATHS_ROOT=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R/library`
   - `R_LIBS=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R`
:::


### `hpc slurm`

SLURM is a popular program used by HPCs to allocate compute resources.
The `hpc slurm` command sets up several utility scripts for interacting with the Slurm workload manager, placing them in `~/.local/bin`.

To set this up, run the following command (also part of `setupmjr hpc`):

```bash
setupmjr hpc slurm
```

The commands are as follows (run `<command> --help` for usage information on each, e.g. `slurm-sbatch --help`):

- `slurm-sbatch`: Submits a SLURM job using `sbatch` and logs the submission details, including the submitted script contents and standard output, into a specified or default log directory (`_tmp/log/sbatch`).
- `slurm-sintx`: Starts an interactive SLURM session using `sintx`. By default, it requests 2 tasks (`--ntasks=2`) and 1 node (`--nodes=1`). You can specify the number of tasks as the first argument, and pass additional flags to `sintx` thereafter (e.g., `slurm-sintx 4 --mem=10G`).
- `slurm-squeue`: Lists the current jobs for the logged-in user using `squeue -u $USER`.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The `hpc slurm` command sets up these tools by doing the following:

1. It ensures that `~/.local/bin` is added to your system's `PATH` environment variable by (if required) adding an export statement to your `.bashrc`.

2. It places the specific utility wrapper scripts (`slurm-sbatch`, `slurm-sintx`, `slurm-squeue`) directly into `~/.local/bin/`.
:::

### `hpc apptainer`

Apptainer (formerly Singularity) is a container system commonly used on HPCs to ensure reproducible software environments. 
The `hpc apptainer` command sets up several utility scripts for seamlessly pulling, locating, and interacting with Apptainer containers.
It is designed to work tightly with images built using the `MiguelRodo/devcontainer-prebuild` GitHub Action, sharing many of the same conventions (but is compatible with containers from both Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry).

To set this up, run the following command (also part of `setupmjr hpc`):

```bash
setupmjr hpc apptainer
```

The commands installed are as follows (run `<command> --help` for usage information on each, e.g. `apptainer-run --help`):

- `apptainer-pull`: Downloads Docker or GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) images and saves them as `.sif` files. It cleverly infers the appropriate repository owner, image name, and tag dynamically based on your current directory's Git remote and active branch.
- `apptainer-path`: Automatically locates the relevant `.sif` file for your current project. It searches Apptainer cache and `/scratch` directories, prioritizing image names that match your current directory's basename and active Git branch.
- `apptainer-exists`: A utility script that checks if the required `.sif` container for the current workspace has already been downloaded, returning a clean exit (0) if found.
- `apptainer-run`: Executes a given command inside the project's Apptainer container. If no command is passed, it falls back to opening an interactive shell (`apptainer shell`) within the container.
- `apptainer-rscript`: A specialized wrapper to easily pass and execute R expressions (via `Rscript -e`) directly inside the project's container without needing to manually spin up an interactive shell.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The `hpc apptainer` command sets up these tools by doing the following:

1. It ensures that `~/.local/bin` is added to your system's `PATH` environment variable by (if required) adding an export statement to your `.bashrc`.

2. It places the specific utility wrapper scripts directly into `~/.local/bin/`.
:::


### `hpc r`

To configure `R` for the HPC environment, run the following command (which is also part of `setupmjr hpc`):

```bash
setupmjr hpc r
```

This command simply calls `setupmjr r`, which configures `radian` and `lintr`.

For full details on how this works and how it configures your environment, please refer to the [R setup documentation](r.qmd).

You can also pass `--not-radian` or `--not-lintr` to opt out of those configurations:

```bash
setupmjr hpc r --not-lintr
```
